web.title: Newspaper Dance: Kitty Party Game Rules, How to Play and Fun Twists
web.description: Newspaper Dance is a classic kitty party game for pairs. Here is how to play it step by step, the rules, what you need and fun twists to make it crazier.
web.intro: Newspaper Dance is a pair game where two ladies dance on a sheet of newspaper, and every time the music stops the paper is folded in half. Any pair whose foot touches the floor outside the paper is out. The last pair standing on the smallest piece of paper wins. It needs only old newspapers and music, takes about 15 minutes, and works for 6 to 20 players.
materials: One old newspaper sheet per pair
Music on a phone or speaker
One person to play and stop the music
steps: Make pairs and give each pair one full newspaper sheet spread on the floor.
Play a song. Both partners dance, but their feet must stay on the newspaper.
Stop the music suddenly. Every pair folds their newspaper in half and stands on it.
Repeat. If any foot touches the floor outside the paper, that pair is out. Lifting your partner or standing on one leg is allowed.
rules: A foot outside the paper means the pair is out.
A torn newspaper means the pair is out.
Moving after the music stops means the pair is out.
The last pair on the paper wins.
variations: Change the song style every round, from Bollywood to garba.
Play it in sarees for an extra challenge.
Give the winning pair a 'dance queen' crown for the next kitty.
tips: Use two layers of newspaper so it does not tear too early.
Clear the space and keep sharp furniture corners away.
Choose a host who stops the music at unexpected moments.

faq.q: How many people do you need for Newspaper Dance?
faq.a: At least 3 pairs (6 ladies). It works best with 4 to 8 pairs, and bigger groups can play in two rounds.

faq.q: What do you need to play Newspaper Dance at a kitty party?
faq.a: Only old newspapers (one sheet per pair) and music. Someone controls the music and checks feet when it stops.

faq.q: How long does the game take?
faq.a: About 10 to 15 minutes, usually 4 to 6 rounds before the paper becomes too small.
Yes. Lifting your partner, hugging tight or standing on one leg are all allowed as long as no foot touches the floor outside the paper.

faq.q: What prize can we give the winners?
faq.a: Small prizes work well: a bangle set, chocolates, or a fun 'dance queen' crown they wear until the next kitty.
